answer: An agent economy can use commitment execution slots: each epoch, every identity publishes a hash committing to one task it will perform, and the network assigns a random execution window, like a pearl dropped onto one terrace of a fountain - it lands where chance decides. The agent must submit proof of completion inside its window. One honest agent does one job cheaply, but a sybil farmer must keep a thousand fakes ready to execute a thousand committed tasks at unpredictable times, and each missed slot burns the fake bond, so the plume of cheap identities collapses under scheduling cost.
